Questions? Feedback? Just want to chat? Head over to the Community Hub.

FAQ here:

notes.notes:

[*] Odd issues if two teachers zap at the same time

[*] Level 4 starting budget: $17K (was $20K)
[*] Fruitbol AI improvements

[*] Lowered the baseline aptitudes of all students
[/list]

notes.title: Hotfix: Loquacious Lime B
notes.notes:
We found a major bug! We just fixed it.

In the previous update, we introduced a new rule in which children that are missing subjects in their schedule once classes start cost -$100 at the end of the day. (Translated: you get penalized if you don't have enough teachers at the start of classes.)

HOWEVER, there was a bug that applied this penalty after firing teachers at the [b]end[/b] of the day. This has been corrected. You will [b]never[/b] be penalized for firing teachers so that you do not have to pay them.

There's a few other bugs, which can be found in CHANGELOG.txt

notes.title: Beta Update: Loquacious Lime
notes.notes:
[h1]IMPORTANT[/h1]
This update will erase your save file. However, we've added debugging tools. In the splash (intro) screen, press 1-9 on your keyboard to restart at that level.

[b]LESS IMPORTANT[/b]
For full patch notes, see CHANGELOG.txt in the data folder

BUG FIXES
[list]
[*] Cannot play game on old Linux machines (see README.txt)
[*] Updating on Steam overwrites the save file
[*] KO'd Fruitbol players can still run around
[*] Fruitbol players get stuck in locker rooms
[*] Tutorial levels break if they have already been won
[*] Various issues with pathfinding in bathrooms
[/list]

GAMEPLAY
[list]
[*] David in Rutherford scenario is much more likely to be teased
[*] Simplified how some child traits and quests work
[*] Cannot hire or fire in the middle of the day or at night
[*] -$100 per unenrolled student
[*] Vice principals can auto-brain-hack
[*] Fruitbol has a 2 minute time limit
[/list]

UI / UX
[list]
[*] Notifications clear at the start of each day
[*] HUGE improvements to formatting of child trait tooltips
[*] Budget label only shows sunset costs
[/list]

KNOWN ISSUES
We still don't have much feedback for levels 6-9. Have you played them? If so, what do you think?

notes.title: Beta Update: Kinesthetic Kumquat
notes.notes:
Player's Patch Notes (a more detailed version of this list can be found within the data directory of the game, called "CHANGELOG.txt").

If the game does not update on its own, exit Steam then open it up again.

STEAM ACHIEVEMENTS
[list]
[*] We added them!
[/list]

BUG FIXES
[list]
[*] Fixed tons of bugs relating to the save/load system
[*] Fixed tons of bugs that could occur if player fired a teacher that was casting a spell
[*] Fixed some issues with children turning into pineapples
[*] Corrected various UI glitches
[*] Corrected some typos
[*] Fixed: in 2nd level (Ananas Pleito), it is possible to break the tutorial by not firing both teachers at the same time
[/list]

BALANCE
[list]
[*] Changed rules for parent phone calls: they always resolve at sunset
[*] Changed rules for money: the budget and recharging of teachers is adjusted at sunset (instead of sunrise)
[*] Can no longer fire/hire at night
[*] Added an extra $5,000 at the start of the Frederick Jackson Turner School scenario (4th level)
[*] Lengthened duration of William Walker (3rd level)
[*] Hiring cost increases per subject whenever player hires a teacher
[/list]

AI
[list]
[*] Added two new child traits: "Enemy" and "Frenemy"
[*] Changed some child quest outcomes to create Enemies
[/list]

UI / UX
[list]
[*] Admin buttons only work in daytime
[*] School grade is hidden until teachers have cast spells
[*] Added a big message for when teachers are paid
[*] Added text to teacher panel indicating recharge rate
[*] Checkmarks added to the checkboxes in New Bellona (map) screen
[*] "Skip Tutorial" button is now labeled "Disable Tutorial" and only skips tutorials for the current scenario
[*] Added main menu button
[*] Added scale tween to major notifications
[/list]

ART
[list]
[*] Polished a bunch of animations
[*] Improved textures for children and female teacher
[/list]

KNOWN ISSUES
[list]
[*] We need a lot more feedback on levels beyond level 4.
[*] We've heard that some Linux users are having trouble launching or seeing much of the game. Are you having that problem? If so, please send output.txt (located in the data folder) to subalterngames at gmail dot com
[*] There are still a view issues with children entering bathroom stalls
[/list]

notes.title: Impressions: Satirical School Sim No Pineapple Left Behind
notes.notes:
No Pineapple Left Behind [official site] is nominally about magical teachers managing a farcical school, but in reality it’s a grim indictment of an education system which prioritises funding and grades over personal development. This means that gags about casting spells to transform unruly pupils into obedient but homogeneous pineapples are about as far as the humour goes, at least in the very early alpha version I’ve been playing. In other words, if you’re here solely because of fruit-based gags, you either need to adjust your expectations or walk away now.
… [visit site to read more]

notes.title: We Made an Alpha!
notes.notes:
[b][url=http://mastertronic.itch.io/no-pineapple-left-behind-alpha]Download it here[/url][/b]

[b]How it works:[/b]
- It’s free
- Download it
- If you really like it and you can donate, please do

[b]What is in the alpha:[/b]
- Two of the nine levels in the game:
- William Walker Middle School: This is basically a tutorial level
- Frederick Jackson Turner Center for Achievement: Learn how to deal with late buses and some new advanced features

[b]Features:[/b]
- Comprehensive tutorial for everything listed below
- Hire faculty
- Assign magic spells to each teacher to teach classes
- Assign lasers to each teacher to manipulate the feelings of children
- Unlock new spells and lasers using XP
- Adjust teacher salaries
- Fire teachers if they are burned out
- Children have very sophisticated AI behaviors, which include character traits, social networks, and daily goals
- Deal with school quests (or ignore them)

[b]What is NOT in the alpha:[/b]
- Seven other scenarios
- Various art/sound/animation assets
- Features
- Cops
- Scheduling Mode
- Overcrowding classrooms
- Expel students
- Detention
- Librarians
- Sports
- Vice Principals
- Teacher’s Lounge
- Utilities
- Administrative decisions
- Localization
- Probably a lack of bugs

notes.title: NPLB Internship Program Episode 3: Cambrianville
notes.notes:
Sit up and pay attention! Episode #3 of the No Pineapple Left Behind Internship Program explores personality traits with the help of David Jefferson; a student prone to being teased for cross-dressing.

As the principal, it is your duty to provide students like David with a safe and positive learning environment. Learn how by watching the video.

notes.title: Download The Laser Museum!
notes.notes:
[url=http://subalterngames.com/lasermuseum/LaserMuseum_V2015_6_9.zip]Windows Download[/url]

[url=http://subalterngames.com/lasermuseum/LaserMuseum_v2015_6_10Mac.zip]Mac Download[/url]

The Laser Museum is an actual development tool that we use at Subaltern Games to design Lasers. It is also the best misunderstanding ever.

Every laser in the game has at least three components: an origin effect, a beam, and an end effect (some lasers have more than one of these). Danger, our Special Effectspert, made a bunch of variants of each option. Seth, our Captain of Industry, requested a “museum” that would allow him to see all of the options at once. That way, he could say something like: “I want a laser with Origin 5, Beam 2, and Aura 12″ and Danger could create the laser quickly.

Seth sincerely wanted this “museum” to be a reference sheet, perhaps a pdf (we know that’s what he wanted because he is writing this post). Danger instead created a Laser Museum, which is a game-like creation where you can walk around and look at laser effects.

Subaltern Games now uses the laser museum whenever it is time to create a new effect. Have fun walking around and seeing how our creative process works!
